title: Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
• Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
• Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
• Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
• Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
• Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
• Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
• Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
• Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
• Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
• Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.


A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work a flexible work schedule including evenings, overnights, and weekends
- 1+ years of electrical facilities maintenance, or 1+ years of mechanical facilities

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience

You'll partner with Operations leadership to weave safety into the fabric of our daily operations, using data-driven insights to create innovative solutions that reduce risk and enhance productivity. Your ability to build trust, influence change, and drive results will be crucial as you lead comprehensive risk assessments and transform safety data into actionable strategies.
Leadership is at the heart of this role. You'll build and develop a high-performing team of WHS professionals, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and excellence.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Leadership & Innovation - Transform safety culture through leadership and innovative solutions. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that set new benchmarks in workplace safety. Leverage technology and data analytics to drive preventive safety measures that protect our associates while enhancing operational excellence. Develop leadership plans, communicate expectations, and drive initiatives to create a safe work environment. Measure performance against WHS policies, analyze metrics, and conduct site audits to address non-compliance issues.

Strategic Partnership & Influence - Build partnerships with Operations leadership to integrate safety into every aspect of our business. Use compelling data analysis and risk insights to influence positive change and drive strategic decision-making. Establish yourself as a trusted advisor who balances safety excellence with operational demands. Oversee recordkeeping, workplace organization, and WHS training programs.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies

- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

title: Senior UX Designer, Design
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Business stands at the intersection of tech & retail in the B2B space developing innovative purchasing and procurement solutions to help businesses and organizations thrive. The Amazon Business User Experience team champions the business customer in the Amazon Marketplace and supports procurement elements for Amazon Business customers. Areas that a Senior UX Designer in AB team will support include partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver costumer-centric solutions for admins involved in business procurement for all sizes of businesses. You will work with the foundational services team to enhance the account management tools in the account configuration and analytics space.

A Senior UX Designer in this organization works on the tactical and strategic. They determine the strategy and where to simplify or extend solutions for the best outcome. They will drive the use of best practices and learn to influence and force multiply. This role needs to be capable of operating autonomously in partnering with product stakeholders from the enterprise account management team to research, define requirements and realize solutions for complex problems across the end-to-end account admins experience. This role will be instrumental in defining the agentic experiences leveraging latest AI technologies.

Key job responsibilities
The Senior UX Designer's role is to facilitate process where there is ambiguity in product strategy, product requirements, and technical feasibility. They will be expected to pull insights, guide product stakeholders into design exercises and activities to shape and prioritize user stories ahead of designing solutions. This role must be able to recognize risks and effectively communicate and escalate issues that may impact the customer experience, then help to arrive at solutions that are acceptable to cross-functional stakeholders - be it peers or skip-level. This role is a key contributor to generating design documents that succinctly communicate recommendations, limitations, trade-offs and product direction to leaders across the org. This role must be able to articulate potential consequences of short-term solutions that may negatively impact customers. Where there are opportunities, a Senior UX Designer must propose optimal long-term solutions as methods of inventing and simplifying for the greatest impact in delivery. This role will be instrumental in helping to inform and shape product roadmaps, business goals, objectives and metrics that all add customer value.

A day in the life
The Senior UX Designer is a vocal advocate for the customer, and they will work on multiple initiatives concurrently. This role operates as an ambassador for best practices, impactful trends, and continually innovates on released features. This role will be a highly visible team player through their ability to pull stakeholders together to collaborate. As a Sr. UX designer and champion of people, their mentoring will include critiquing, providing design feedback, conducting retros & research that can influence engineering team decisions to enable optimal solutions for our customers.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of UX designer or interaction designer experience
- Have an online portfolio or samples of work on resume, demonstrating experience creating great end-to-end, user-centered design solutions and patterns, across desktop and mobile devices
- Experience in delivering design solutions for projects of large scope and complexity
- Experience working with stakeholders to plan and execute programs that are strategic in nature
- Experience using customer insights and data to deeply understand target customers and dive deep
- Experience in a variety of design, wire-framing, and prototyping tools

Preferred qualifications

- Experience applying scrum to visual or UX design processes
- Master's degree or equivalent in design, human-computer interaction (HCI), or Master's degree
- Experience in B2B, high-tech products/services preferred
- Experience developing, deploying and managing AI products at scale

title: Software Development Engineer, Measurement, Ad Tech, and Data Science (MADS) Foundations- Traffic
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Ads Traffic ingests hundreds of billions of ad events daily, decorates them with dimensional and identity data, and publishes the structured traffic and billing datasets that the entire Ads measurement ecosystem depends on — including three of the five critical metrics used for Ads billing. You'll design and deliver features across Spark-based EMR pipelines, decoration jobs, and publication systems that operate under strict tier-one SLAs for data freshness and accuracy.

The Traffic Applications team, part of Measurement, AdTech, and Data Science (MADS), is the first system in the MADS stack to encounter regulatory and identity changes — meaning the architectural decisions made here propagate across the entire measurement pipeline. You'll work on high-visibility initiatives that directly impact Ads VP and SVP-level goals, including compliance work (GDPR, ePrivacy), geo-targeting features, and architecture scalability to support spiky traffic from live sports events.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop features across Spark-based EMR pipelines, decoration jobs, and publication systems that process hundreds of billions of ad events daily
- Deliver end to end across the full development lifecycle — from requirements and system design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations under tier-one SLAs
- Navigate technical problems with competing constraints — regulatory deadlines, performance requirements, cost targets, and cross-org dependencies — and propose well-reasoned solutions
- Collaborate with engineers across Ads, Customer Trust, and identity-owning upstream systems to ensure Traffic's design decisions support downstream consumers
- Contribute to compliance initiatives (GDPR, ePrivacy) and scalability efforts for high-traffic events like live sports
- Maintain sound operational practices — alarms, telemetry, runbooks — for a system where data freshness and accuracy directly impact billing
- Mentor peers through design reviews, code reviews, and knowledge sharing

A day in the life
On a typical day you might start with a stand-up to align on priorities, then dive into building or extending a Spark pipeline to handle a new decoration requirement. After lunch, you could be debugging a data freshness issue against a tier-one SLA, tracing it through the ingestion path to a root cause. Between coding, you'll review pull requests, participate in design discussions for upcoming compliance or scalability work, and collaborate with downstream consumers to understand how they use your datasets.

About the team
The Traffic Applications team owns the data ingress system for all of Amazon Ads — ingesting hundreds of billions of ad events daily, decorating them with dimensional and identity data, and publishing structured traffic and billing datasets to consumers across the Ads ecosystem. The system operates under strict SLAs for data freshness and accuracy on tier-one advertising metrics, owning three of the five metrics used for billing. As the first MADS system to encounter regulatory and identity changes, Traffic's architectural decisions propagate across the entire MADS stack, making design choices here uniquely consequential.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: テクニカルアカウントマネージャー / Technical Account Manager (TAM), Digital Innovation
descriptionHtml:
スタートアップからエンタープライズに至る日本の多くの企業が、クラウド技術を活用してビジネス上のアドバンテージを得ようとしています。これに伴い、技術や運用に関してガイダンスを提供し、お客様のクラウドジャーニーに伴走するエキスパートが求められています。AWS エンタープライズサポートでは、お客様の変革を支援し、クラウドジャーニーの各フェーズでお客様の最も近くにいる担当者であるTechnical Account Manager(TAM)を募集しています。

Technical Account Manager (TAM)は、お客様がAWS上で技術的なソリューションを実現するための支援、またそれを運用していく中でお客様が直面する様々な課題の解決の支援を行います。お客様は、デジタルネイティブと呼ばれる企業群、SaaS アプリケーション提供企業から、伝統ある日本企業、複数の業種にまたがる大企業、そしていまや公共団体にまで拡がっています。お客様の急速な成長と共にエンタープライズサポートの組織も成長しており、そのスピードに合わせTAMはクラウドジャーニーの様々なステージにいる数社のお客様を同時に支援します。なお、TAMは、金融、製造、流通、サービス、テレコム、メディア、ゲーム、ISVといった業界のエンドカスタマー、もしくはパートナー のいずれかの業界のお客様をご担当いただきます。

TAMは、お客様が抱える技術的に難しい課題の解決を支援し、必要に応じてお客様に技術的なガイダンスを提供、そして、お客様のシステムアーキテクチャやオペレーションに対して技術的なレビューをします。それらに加えて、TAMは 日本を含めた グローバルの AWS 内でお客様の代弁者として行動する事が期待されています。この仕事を通じて、あなたはお客様のシステムアーキテクチャや技術的オペレーションに習熟しながら、お客様との間に強いプロフェッショナルな信頼関係を築く事ができるでしょう。

これまでTAMとして採用された候補者の多くは、ネットワーク、データベース、アプリケーションサーバー、オペレーティングシステム、プログラミングといったインターネットを利用したサービスに関係する技術に対する経験を持ち、それらのうち１つ以上の分野に習熟しています。過去のクラウドコンピューティングの経験は必須ではありません。また、開発や社内情報システム部門で活躍されていた方も採用され、活躍しています。入社後には、AWSに関する専門的な技術を習得するための3ヶ月にわたるトレーニングが提供され提供されるため、AWS初心者の方でも安心してご入社いただけます。

AWS を活用した大規模なワークロードをサポートできるやりがいのある職種です。フレックスタイム制度などの柔軟な働き方と、入社後研修後も定期的に提供されるラーニングの機会、そして将来のキャリアの選択肢も幅広くあります。

AWS におけるお客様の代弁者として、お客様と日本のビジネスに貢献するこの魅力的なロールにチャレンジしてみませんか。


Key job responsibilities
- AWS エンタープライズ サポートのテクニカル アカウント マネージャとして、お客様の Point of Contact として活動し、お客様の困難な技術的課題に対して AWS の幅広いサービスの知識とテクニカルリソースを駆使してその課題の解決を支援する。また、重要なイベントが発生した際にお客様とのコミュニケーションを先導
- お客様との信頼関係を構築・維持向上し、お客様のビジネスニーズや技術的な課題を理解
- お客様のシステムやオペレーションに対して技術面およびコスト面のレビューを定期的に提供し、より適切なサービスや機能を提案
- トレーニングや勉強会を通じて新サービス情報やAWS のベストプラクティスを提供し、お客様がそれを咀嚼し正しく活用できるよう支援
- お客様から AWS サポートに寄せられたサポートケースを把握し、サポートエンジニアと協業してAWS 各部門へエスカレーションし、問題の解決を促進するとともに、お客様がその問題についてお客様社内関係者や上位層に正しくかつタイムリーに報告できるよう支援
- お客様のニーズを把握し、それを満たすためのより良いサービスや機能の提案を行うことで、よりお客様のビジネスにAWSが役立つよう促す。またお客様のビジネスを阻害する問題がAWS側にあれば、それを検知し、他のTAMや部門と協業してその解消を促進
- AWS の Solution Architects, Professional Services, Sales Account Managers とアカウントチームとして協業し、またアカウントチームとしての活動の一部を担う。
- チーム内の知識や経験の蓄積を推進し、チームメンバーの能力開発に貢献

descriptionHtml:

title: Sr. Software Development Manager, Outbound Agentic Marketing Demand
descriptionHtml:
Outbound is re-imagining the communications and marketing landscape with generative and agentic AI, changing how millions of customers discover products and engage with brands across Amazon.com and beyond.

Amazon reaches shoppers billions of times through email, mobile push, SMS, and other messaging channels. We're turning that into a marketplace. Each shopper's limited attention is the supply. The messages that compete for it, and the marketers, category leaders, and AI agents who create them, are the demand. A separate team runs the auction that decides which message earns each moment. This role builds the demand side: everything that determines how good, how varied, and how dependable the content and campaigns entering that marketplace are.

Today, most marketing email still looks like a catalog printout, and the tools behind it make ambitious creative slow and fragile. We want Amazon's messages to have the visual quality of the best brand content on social, and to be relevant to the specific moment a customer is in. A customer getting into cycling, or planning a first camping trip, should get a story-led series built for that interest, not a generic deal alert. Picture a feed: AI agents continuously generate on-brand, category-specific content from customer and category signals, and the marketplace decides what each customer sees and when. Your team makes that inventory rich, high quality, and trustworthy.

As the Senior Manager, Software Development for Generative Marketing & Demand, you'll build and lead an organization of software engineers, working closely with applied scientists and design technologists. You'll own:
- The authoring platform (open source). A toolkit that takes a design from Figma, a brief in Slack, or a contributor's draft and produces finished, accessible, on-brand content for email, push, and long-form article pages. It covers a shared component and design-token spec, a compiler that produces inbox-safe output that renders as designed in every client, automated checks (accessibility, size, links, deliverability, brand rules), real-client previews, and in-thread review and approval. We intend to build the core in the open under a permissive license, so the industry's best email and design-tool engineers can improve it alongside us, while Amazon's customer data, brand, and sending systems plug in privately through adapters.

- Generative and agentic content. Agents that draft, adapt, and localize creative, generate lifestyle imagery for catalog products, write copy in a brand's voice, and assemble category-specific stories and drip series from customer and category signals and from opportunities the marketplace sends back. Every generated piece passes the same gates as human work before it reaches a customer.

- Campaign planning and execution. The tools marketing teams use to plan, configure, schedule, and operate campaigns and coordinated waves of campaigns, including peak events like Prime Day. The bar is simple: what a marketer plans is what customers get. Operators see the effective send window, the policies that apply (quiet hours, cadence, consent, channel limits), and a reconciled funnel from audience to delivery, with the reason behind every number, before and during a send rather than in a retro afterward.

- Data and audience connectors. A pluggable, documented mechanism for bringing in audiences, catalog and deal data, recommendations, and third-party sources, with timeouts, fallbacks, and validation, so new data sources can be added without platform changes. Connectors built by Amazon teams and by the open-source community use the same contract.

- Send-path reliability. Low-latency, high-throughput content rendering and handoff to Amazon's sending infrastructure at peak-event volumes, with verifiable delivery: every send is traceable, auditable, and reconciles with what was planned.



Key job responsibilities
- Build, hire, and grow a high-performing team of software engineers, including senior and principal engineers and, as the organization scales, managers. Set a high hiring bar and develop the next generation of technical leaders.
- Own the Generative Marketing & Demand vision, roadmap, and multi-year plan (OP1/OP2) with product, design, science, and marketing partners. Turn an ambiguous goal, best-in-class creative and campaign tooling in an industry with strong commercial incumbents, into a delivery plan with measurable milestones.
- Lead the open-source program for the authoring platform. Work with Amazon's open-source office and Legal on licensing and the open/private boundary. Build the community mechanisms that make it a multi-party project rather than an Amazon-only one: public roadmap, RFC process for spec changes, contribution and code-review standards, conformance tests, release management, security response, and named maintainers inside and outside Amazon. Recruit external maintainers and early adopters (other companies, agencies, ESPs, and design-tool developers), and measure the project's health by external contributors and downstream adoption.
- Hold a clear architectural line between open and private: nothing in the open core depends on Amazon systems, no customer data flows through open code paths, and Amazon runs the released open packages rather than a fork.
- Be accountable for outcomes. Creative quality and relevance (engagement, conversion, and incremental lift against holdouts), brief-to-approved-content time, rendering and accessibility defects, plan-versus-actual send accuracy, and marketer adoption are the measures. Opens alone are not.
- Partner with applied scientists on content generation, creative quality scoring, category and interest modeling, and the signals that tell agents which content to create for which customer moment. Move models from research to production quickly and safely.
- Partner with the marketplace team so that content, metadata, and quality signals flow cleanly into the attention auction, and opportunity signals flow back to content agents.
- Make AI-generated content safe by default: brand, legal, claims, accessibility, and deliverability checks block publishing automatically; human reviewers focus on judgment; prompts and outputs are logged; and responsible-AI, privacy, and communications compliance requirements (CAN-SPAM, TCPA, GDPR, consent) are non-negotiable.
- Drive adoption across a broad set of internal tenants, including Retail, Prime, Prime Video, Music, Alexa, and Ads marketing teams, and category leaders who contribute long-form content. Meet them in the tools they already use (Figma, Slack, documents, CLI, and agent clients via MCP) rather than asking them to learn a new console.
- Own operational excellence: on-call health, alarming, COEs, security reviews, service-level goals, and peak-event readiness, including during Prime Day, Prime Big Deal Days, and the holidays.
- Communicate clearly in writing and in reviews with senior leadership, including narratives, PR/FAQs, and business reviews, and represent Amazon externally in the open-source and email-engineering communities.

A day in the life
You might start with the open-source triage: an external contributor's pull request fixes a dark-mode rendering bug in a new mail-client release, and another company has proposed an RFC to extend the spec for interactive modules. Then you'd review the weekly metrics: a category storytelling pilot for outdoor gear is showing incremental new-to-category customers against its holdout, and brief-to-approved time dropped below a day. After that, you'd walk a marketing lead through a readiness review for the next peak event, where the wave view shows every campaign's effective send window and flags one that a channel quiet-hour rule will cut short, so it gets fixed before the event instead of during it. In the afternoon, you'd join a design review for a new connector contract with your principal engineer, meet with an applied scientist on why generated lifestyle imagery is drifting off-brand for one category, and close an offer for a senior engineer who found the team through the open-source project.

About the team
We're a high-ownership team in Outbound Communications, building the tools that decide how good Amazon's messages can be. We build from first principles, work in the open where it makes the product better, and hold to one rule: every message has to be worth the customer's attention.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of engineering team management experience
- 10+ years of planning, designing, developing and delivering consumer software experience
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams
- Experience managing multiple concurrent programs, projects and development teams in an Agile environment

Preferred qualifications

title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Shopping Personalization AI
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Personalization organization builds the AI systems behind how hundreds of millions of customers discover and shop. We extract and reason over customer signals in real time, power LLM-driven recommendation experiences, and build AI-native discovery surfaces that combine products, content, and contextual recommendations. Our work sits at the intersection of generative AI, large-scale distributed systems, and customer-facing products, delivered through high-performance web and mobile experiences at Amazon scale.

In this role you'll design and build features that shape how customers discover products - tailored to their preferences, helping them find exactly what they need, even before they know they need it. We're defining how LLMs integrate into real-time personalization, how noisy behavioral signals become durable customer understanding, and how AI-powered experiences ship reliably at scale. You'll work across multiple technical teams, ship iteratively, and see your work in the hands of customers quickly. This organization values experimentation, moves fast, and gives engineers real ownership over what they build.

We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer who leads through technical depth and sound judgment. Someone who owns team-level architecture, provides system-wide design guidance, and brings perspective on both current and future technology choices. You take on customer problems where the technological strategy is not yet defined, and you drive productive discussions to align teams on the best path forward. You don’t just deliver high-quality software yourself - you set the standard that others follow. You actively mentor multiple engineers, drive adoption of engineering best practices, and ensure your team has strong operational foundations. You make the team permanently stronger, not dependent on your presence. title: Embedded Software Engineer II, Ring, Ring Firmware
descriptionHtml:
Ring is growing in Poland and we are looking for experienced Embedded Software Engineers to join our team in Gdansk. You will work on firmware for IoT devices used by millions of customers worldwide, developing new features and shipping products from concept to production.

As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will own the design and implementation of firmware subsystems running on resource-constrained hardware. You will work across the full development cycle: architecture, implementation, code review, testing on real devices, and production release. Our team operates with high autonomy and a strong feedback culture.

The ideal candidate:

Has shipped embedded products to production and understands what it takes to go from prototype to millions of devices in the field.
Writes clean, maintainable C/C++ for constrained environments and cares deeply about code quality.
Communicates proactively, raises technical risks early, and drives solutions across teams.
Thrives in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift as customer needs evolve.
Is curious about the full stack, from hardware registers to cloud connectivity, and enjoys learning new domains.

Key job responsibilities
Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware in C/C++ for Ring devices.
Specify and implement functionality for embedded subsystems (connectivity, streaming, power management, sensors, or security).
Collaborate with hardware, QA, cloud, and app teams to deliver integrated product experiences.
Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, and cross-team architecture decisions.
Debug complex issues across hardware and software boundaries using JTAG, UART, and protocol analyzers.

A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing a code change from a colleague working on a new sensor driver. After your team standup, you spend focused time implementing a feature for an upcoming product launch, testing it on real hardware at your desk. In the afternoon, you dig into a tricky issue that only reproduces on one board variant, tracing it from application code down to a register misconfiguration. You push your fix, verify it on the device, and close the day knowing it will ship to customers in the next release.

- BA/BS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related field, or equivalent practical experience

title: Principal Tech Program Manager, AWS Hardware Engineering Services
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead cross-organizational hardware component initiatives within our Core Hardware Engineering organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for the full lifecycle of mechanical and electrical components that power the entire AWS server fleet, from early architecture and design through manufacturing readiness, production ramp, and long-term fleet sustainment.

About the Role
Core Hardware Engineering is a horizontal organization that provides foundational hardware engineering capabilities across multiple vertical product lines within AWS Infrastructure. The mechanical portfolio includes fans, heatsinks, liquid cooling systems, cold plates, quick disconnects, chassis, rack frames, cables, and connectors. The electrical portfolio includes motherboards, power boards, system boards, PCIe switches and retimers, CPUs, and memory. As a Principal Technical Program Manager, you will own the strategy and delivery of component-level outcomes that serve every server platform in the AWS fleet.

What You Will Do
You will define and deliver complex component initiatives with broad cross-organizational impact in areas where business and architectural strategy has not yet been established. Your work begins before vertical server programs are formally defined and extends through manufacturing and long-term fleet sustainment, an end-to-end lifecycle span unique to this role.

You will own a portfolio spanning multiple component domains, dozens of active qualifications, concurrent technology transitions, and fleet-wide operations. You will orchestrate deliverables across multiple hardware engineering teams, managing prioritization and trade-offs between design, new product introduction, manufacturing, and sustaining operations to ensure engineering capacity is allocated against the highest-impact work.

You will drive strategic supplier relationships to reduce component lead times, establishing joint development roadmaps, negotiating capacity commitments ahead of demand signals, and creating multi-source qualification paths. You will hold commitments across vertical product teams, data center operations, manufacturing test teams, and external vendors, establishing scalable mechanisms for roadmap inspection, manufacturing readiness reviews, and cross-team dependency tracking that operate independently of your direct involvement.

You will deliver four primary outcomes: entitlement performance, manufacturing readiness, annualized failure rate and unsellable performance, and supply continuity, translating directly into platform readiness, cost reduction, and stability at scale.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Experience managing the full hardware product lifecycle from design through manufacturing ramp and sustaining operations.
- Experience driving cross-organizational programs spanning multiple engineering teams, manufacturing operations, and external suppliers.
- Experience with component-level hardware development including mechanical and electrical systems.
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

Preferred qualifications

- 8+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Direct experience with server or data center hardware at scale, including familiarity with ODM and JDM engagement models.
- Experience driving supplier development strategies, including joint development roadmaps, capacity planning, and multi-source qualification.
- Demonstrated ability to operate with complete independence in ambiguous environments where business and architectural strategy has not yet been defined.
- Experience establishing organizational mechanisms such as roadmap reviews, manufacturing readiness reviews, and supplier business reviews that persist and scale beyond individual involvement.
- Track record of delivering measurable business outcomes tied to total cost of ownership, time-to-market, manufacturing yield, and fleet reliability.
- Experience with firmware and software integration as it relates to hardware component readiness and platform bring-up.
- Master's degree in Engineering or an MBA.

title: Risk and Fraud Manager, Amazon Credit, Amazon LATAM Payments Trust
descriptionHtml:
Own risk and fraud prevention for Amazon Crédito, Amazon's first-party lending product in Brazil, and protect a brand-new credit business from day one. You will map the product journey end-to-end, find where fraudsters and abusers get in, and build the mechanisms that stop them — before losses scale.

This is a builder's role at the intersection of lending, identity, and payment risk. Embedded with the Amazon Crédito team and reporting into Payments Trust's Integrity function, you will help shape the fraud & abuse approach for the product, assess and prioritize risk against a defined risk appetite, ship detection and prevention mechanisms, stand up the metrics that prove they work, and lead the response when new fraud patterns emerge. As Amazon Crédito scales, you are accountable for keeping fraud and abuse loss within acceptable thresholds.

Key job responsibilities
- Map the journey and identify risks. Map the Amazon Crédito customer journey end to end — sign-up, credit-line usage, and post-purchase disputes — pinpoint where fraud and abuse get in, assess exposure by likelihood and impact against the product's risk appetite, and prioritize where controls are needed most.
- Design and support prevention solutions. Know what the market and Amazon offer, and build data-backed business cases that support build-vs-integrate prioritization — partnering with engineering, product, and data teams to ship controls that stop fraud and abuse without friction for legitimate customers.
- Detect emerging fraud patterns and respond to spikes. Build mechanisms that surface new fraud tactics early, set alerts and thresholds, and act quickly to contain losses when a spike happens.
- Set the metrics and track results. Define how success is measured, make the numbers visible in real time, and hold the program to its loss-reduction targets.
- Report progress to leadership. Give clear, data-backed updates on the risks, how controls perform, and what's next.
- Work hand in hand with the Amazon Crédito team. Join their weekly rhythm, build the relationships that make prevention work, and bring the fraud & abuse view into product and business decisions.

A day in the life
You start in the weekly, listening for what's changing in Amazon Crédito and where new exposure is opening up. Mid-morning you dig into a flagged pattern — a cluster of accounts sharing the same device — and decide whether it's a spike worth acting on. After lunch you work with engineering to scope a new identity-check control, then update your metrics dashboard ahead of a leadership review. You close the day drafting a one-pager on an emerging fraud pattern, with a clear recommendation. Some days you're building strategy; some days you're stopping losses in real time. Both matter.

About the team
Amazon LATAM Payments Trust builds the compliance, identity, and fraud & abuse prevention mechanisms that create trust in payment transactions — letting millions of customers transact safely and enabling Amazon to scale new products in a dynamic payments market. We own this end-to-end across the region, from setting strategy to shipping the mechanisms that run in production.
We are a small, senior, high-trust team with a lot of ownership and a strong bias for action. We think in mechanisms, not one-offs; we ground decisions in data; and we care about building things that last and replicate across markets.

Basic qualifications

- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in product, program, or project management in leading cross-functional teams in delivery of major new products or services
- Product management experience

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of SQL and VBA at an advanced level
- Experience building and analyzing cost/benefit scenarios and business cases and communicating results throughout the organization
- Experience and understanding of the workflow within a marketing, production, or creative department or company

title: Commissioning Engineer, AWS Commissioning
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

AWS is looking for a dynamic Commissioning Engineer. It is the responsibility of all Amazonians to have alignment with our leadership principles and demonstrate these at the highest level.

The responsibilities of the ACx Commissioning Engineer (CxE) include, but are not limited to, oversight and coordination of multi-discipline division of work related to design review and commissioning of Amazon critical infrastructure for new construction and special projects. The CxE is responsible for supporting vendors, contractors, and other teams involved in the construction and commissioning of various systems including medium and low voltage power systems, Generators, UPS, HVAC, Chilled Water, BMS, and EPMS systems. They shall provide multi-discipline input into the scheduling, test script development, designing, and planning of projects. In addition, the CxE will be required to develop and review electrical and mechanical component and integrated systems testing along with other commissioning documents to ensure they are compliant with the basis of design, specification, industry standards and sequence of operations. It is the CxE responsibility to ensure that all commissioning procedures follow the appropriate safety practices and policies. CxE is responsible for auditing commissioning activities continuously to ensure compliance with environmental, quality, and safety requirements. The CxE proactively communicates with the ACx Regional Manager and the ACx team to ensure that the applicable test documents are created and executed in accordance with all commissioning requirements. This individual will be responsible for comprehensive weekly reporting of status of all ongoing projects, lessons learned, and program improvements to continually improve the quality of our program. This position will include coverage of multiple inflight projects and tight schedules.

Key job responsibilities
Physical Requirements

• Walk job sites in uneven terrain
• Work at heights and from ladders
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
• Lift and/or move up to 49 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 50 pounds or more
• Carry objects weighing up to 49 pounds for short distances
• Work shifts longer than eight hours in duration with potential for night and weekends
• Perform physical tasks throughout the day without becoming overly tired
• Ability to manipulate small wires and objects easily
• Work in a noisy environment
• Work in environments that are colder or hotter than a normal office environment


Additional Job Requirements

• Ability to relocate to the North Virginia area.
• Ability and willingness to travel domestic and internationally for up to 50% of the year. Typical travel is 20%.
• Required to provide personal transportation for meetings and job visits away from the office; reimbursed.

About the team
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: 2027 Retail Vendor Manager Intern
descriptionHtml:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.
You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

The Amazon University Talent Acquisition Team is looking for ambitious students to join us as Retail Vendor Manager Intern in 2027.

Internship length will be 12 months, full-time.


Key job responsibilities
- Work backwards from the customer, identifying inputs to grow Amazon's most strategic brands and improve their performance within a retail category.
- Support vendor managers in providing a suite of services designed to help brands succeed, collaborating with cross-functional teams including in-stock and marketing.
- Develop analytical and problem-solving skills by collecting, analysing, and interpreting data to drive category performance.
- Build an understanding of customer pain points, requirements, and potential value across retail, advertising, and merchant services.
- Identify target accounts using market data and industry intelligence to support business growth.
- Identify opportunities to improve products, services, processes, systems, and tools across the business.
- Work with different parts of the Amazon business to implement improvement projects, including category teams, product teams, and technical support teams.


A day in the life
Every day is a little different as a Retail Vendor Manager Intern. Working alongside a vendor manager, you'll learn how Amazon handles its e-commerce retail business across product categories — from books to fashion, electronics to grocery, and everything in between. You might spend your morning analysing category performance data and identifying growth opportunities for strategic brands, then spend your afternoon working with marketing or in-stock teams to implement an improvement project that enhances the customer shopping experience.
Amazon is a customer-obsessed business, so no matter which retail category you join, part of your role will involve working backwards from the customer to identify what matters most. You'll gain exposure to Amazon's advertising products and merchant services, learn how we create custom opportunities to delight clients, and partner across functions to deliver results — building your analytical, commercial, and problem-solving skills in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
Note: You must have the right to work in the country of employment by the start date.


About the team
Intern Community:
As an Amazon Intern, you'll be part of a dynamic, supportive community that empowers your growth and development. You'll collaborate with interns from around the world, networking and participating in social events to broaden your perspectives. You can also join specialized groups focused on areas like sustainability to explore your diverse interests.

Support:
The internship program provides a robust support system, including weekly intern office hours, dedicated IT and HR support, and a program team committed to your success. This ensures you have the guidance and assistance needed to thrive.

Learning Sessions:
Exclusive learning sessions will further enhance your skills, granting you access to Amazon's industry-leading learning platforms and the expertise of industry leaders. These structured development opportunities will prepare you for the next step in your career.

Opportunities:
Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.

- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree with a graduation date of Q1 2027 or a recent 2026 graduate (within the last 6 months)

title: Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Construction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative throughout the full construction lifecycle. You play an integral role in delivering the built facilities and infrastructure that power Amazon's logistics network — including sortation centers, delivery stations, and auxiliary buildings — through new builds, retrofits, and expansions.

In this role, you serve as the primary point of interface between Amazon and its external partners — developers, general contractors, design engineers, and authorities having jurisdiction (AHJ) — while collaborating closely with internal stakeholders responsible for equipping, furnishing, and operating our facilities. You are accountable for the safe, on-time, in scope, and on-budget delivery of construction projects, and you bring a disciplined approach to budget management, schedule oversight, contract execution, and quality assurance.

You operate with a high degree of independence within your assigned region, managing multiple concurrent projects while maintaining clear and transparent communication with all project stakeholders. This role combines construction management, engineering, project planning, contract management, and facilities delivery — and requires approximately 60% regional travel within North America.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.

Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Champion Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams; hold all accountable to a safety-first culture
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to maintain regulatory compliance and ensure seamless project execution
- Lead or assist in negotiations with regulatory bodies as required for permitting and approvals

Project & Construction Management
- Manage multiple concurrent projects simultaneously — ranging from small renovations to large-scale ($100M+) new facility builds — from design phase through construction completion and operational handover
- Serve as Amazon's owner's representative and primary integrator between construction execution teams and internal stakeholders (operations, equipment, IT, etc.)
- Review construction documents, drawings, and specifications for conformance to Amazon's building standards and design guidelines
- Identify and resolve design conflicts, schedule clashes, and coordination gaps with other Amazon execution teams
- Conduct detailed reviews of contractor bid packages, budgets, and schedules to identify and resolve discrepancies
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Own comprehensive budget tracking, cashflow forecasting, and cost management across assigned projects
- Review, analyze, and respond to all proposed cost and time change requests submitted by external project teams
- Negotiate construction, procurement, and labor contracts with developers and general contractors; present formal documentation for approval when required
- Ensure contracts are fit for purpose, cost-effective, and incorporate appropriate service level agreements
- Advise on the impact of changes in scope, schedule, cost, and permitting

Contractor & Stakeholder Management
- Audit contractor performance to ensure skills, competencies, and resources are appropriate for the work being performed
- Ensure contracted resources deliver work that meets duration and quality targets; address and resolve underperformance issues
- Coach and guide project teams — including developers, design engineers, general contractors, subcontractors, and internal stakeholders — throughout the full project lifecycle
- Inform developers and contractors of projected changes in resource or work demand to enable proactive planning
- Partner with teams responsible for base building management transition and oversight of all turnover documentation

Communication & Reporting
- Maintain clear, concise, and transparent communication with all internal and external stakeholders on project status, risks, and key developments
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project data
- Participate in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions
- Prepare reports, specifications, and technical analyses to define design requirements, equipment needs, and services for expansion and remodel projects

Innovation & Continuous Improvement
- Provide critical review of current design standards to identify value engineering and design enhancement opportunities
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the construction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Identify and implement process improvements that drive better outcomes across safety, cost, schedule, and quality

A day in the life
Each day, you act as Amazon's owner on the ground — ensuring the safe, on-time, and on-budget execution of construction projects across your region. Your day may include:
- Coordinating with general contractors on project status, upcoming milestones, and emerging risks
- Reviewing and responding to RFIs, submittals, change order requests, and schedule updates
- Participating in AOC meetings and driving accountability across the project team
- Conducting site visits to verify construction quality and safety compliance
- Updating Amazon's project management systems with current budget, schedule, and status information
- Collaborating with internal stakeholders on facility readiness, equipment coordination, and operational handover planning
- Reviewing design documents and providing feedback to engineering and design partner

About the team
At Amazon, the GES NA D&C team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- Experience with AutoCAD and/or Building Information Modeling (BIM), as well as scheduling software (Primavera, MS Project, or similar)
- Experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's project management representative or in other Commercial Development and Construction related disciplines
- 5+ years of project management experience spanning design phase through construction completion and operational handover
- 5+ years of experience negotiating construction, procurement, and/or labor contracts
- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience operating within at least two disciplines within the construction industry, such as Contracting, Owners Representation, Architecture, Design and Engineering, Commercial Development, analysis and control of construction costs or similar
- Experience communicating complex information and solutions to senior stakeholders and influencing decisions
- Experience in facilities management, including planning, design review, implementation, and project controls for new and existing structures
- Experience managing concurrent projects in a program management capacity
- CMIT/CMAA or PMP certification or equivalent

descriptionHtml:

title: Sr. Power Electronics Engineer, Prime Air Electric Propulsion Subsystem
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Sr. Power Electronics Engineer to join our Electric Propulsion Subsystem team. In this role, you will be a significant and autonomous contributor, solving difficult hardware engineering problems related to high-power electronics systems. You will design, develop, and validate power electronics boards from concept through production, working on 10KW+ high-voltage DC systems that push the boundaries of performance, reliability, and efficiency.

This position requires an engineer who demonstrates strong technical depth in power electronics while also exhibiting the system-level thinking and influence characteristic of our most impactful contributors.

Key job responsibilities
• Design, develop, and test multi-layer power electronics board layouts for high-voltage DC systems (10KW+), from initial concept through volume production release.
• Define and execute power electronics component architecture, including topology selection, component specification, and thermal management strategies.
• Lead the development of test plans that validate designs against DO-160 and DO-274 standards, ensuring electromagnetic compatibility, environmental resilience, and functional safety.
• Ensure designs meet appropriate IP (Ingress Protection) ratings for target deployment environments.
• Apply system-level thinking to understand how power electronics subsystems integrate with and influence the broader product architecture.
• Partner effectively with cross-functional peers, suppliers, and contract manufacturers to build and validate designs, driving alignment on technical trade-offs.
• Deliver accurate time-based estimates for engineering tasks and manage design milestones through the product development lifecycle.
• Create and maintain high-quality design documentation including schematics, specifications, analysis reports, and test results.
• Contribute to design reviews, providing constructive technical feedback to teammates and cross-functional partners.
• Identify risks and defects early in the design phase and proactively propose solutions that balance performance, cost, and schedule.
• Improve team processes, tools, and methodologies; develop firmware, software, or scripts that aid development or testing of power electronics hardware.



A day in the life
You independently drive the design and delivery of power electronics hardware, making sound trade-offs between performance, cost, manufacturability, and schedule. Your test plans thoroughly validate designs and efficiently address system integration challenges. You think in terms of the system, not just individual components, and proactively work to improve the overall product architecture. Your work is consistently high quality, meeting safety, regulatory, and reliability standards. You influence your team's technical direction and are recognized as a go-to resource for power electronics expertise.

About the team
The New Experimental Technology (NEXT) Electric Propulsion Subsystem (EPS) organization conducts technology research, design and development of the power system for Prime Air’s drones. We are responsible to deliver an EPS and hardware components that safely supports 15-minute drone delivery and is certifiable by the FAA and EASA regulators.
Our work spans the full product lifecycle, from early-stage research and concept development through detailed design, prototyping, testing, and certification support. The EPS is a critical system enabling Prime Air’s autonomous delivery operations, providing the electrical power generation, storage, distribution, and propulsion capabilities required for safe and reliable flight.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production
- 7+ years of hands-on experience with multi-layer power electronics PCB layout and design.
- 7+ years of experience working on high-voltage DC power systems rated at 10KW or above.
- Demonstrated experience developing power electronics boards from concept through production.
- Proficiency with power electronics design tools (e.g., Altium, OrCAD, ECAD tools, MATLAB/Simulink for power system modeling).

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering or related field
- Experience leading vendor engagements and manufacturing partner discussions for power electronics assemblies.
- Familiarity with thermal simulation, power integrity analysis, and high-voltage creepage/clearance design rules.
- Experience with rapid prototyping techniques and low-volume manufacturing of power electronics hardware.
- Track record of delivering stable, performant hardware solutions that meet cost and quality targets.
- Ability to decompose complex power system challenges into well-defined component-level design tasks.
- Experience with reliability testing, HALT/HASS, and failure analysis of power electronics systems.
- Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions across teams and communicate complex trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.
- Contributions to intellectual property (patents, trade secrets) in the power electronics domain.
- Working knowledge of DO-160 and DO-274 design and test standards.
- Understanding of IP (Ingress Protection) rating requirements and design-for-environment principles

title: Program Manager, Retrofit Expansion and Initiative, Launch and Expansion
descriptionHtml:
About Amazon Japan Operations
Amazon Japan Operations (JP Ops) is responsible for Amazon Japan’s end-to-end logistics and operations in Japan, operating a large-scale, highly integrated supply chain spanning from First Mile to Last Mile. Through Fulfillment Centers (FC), Sort Centers (SC), Delivery Stations (DS), and Sub Same-Day Delivery stations (SSD), we continuously challenge ourselves to deliver packages faster, more reliably, and at lower cost.

About End-to-End Supply Chain & Speed Services
End-to-End Supply Chain & Speed Services is the core organization within JP Ops that owns supply chain strategy as well as network design and execution. By integrating Supply Chain, Network Design/Planning, and Transportation Planning, the organization optimizes forecasting, planning, network flow, and execution in an end-to-end manner. It also leads speed-focused services such as Same-Day Delivery, Quick Commerce, freezer and perishable grocery, and micromobility, enabling rapid innovation at scale to continuously elevate customer experience.

About JP Launch and Expansion (L&E)
JP Launch and Expansion (L&E) is the project management organization under End-to-End Supply Chain & Speed Services that turns supply chain strategy into a real, operating network. L&E owns execution end-to-end—from upstream activities such as site selection, investment return analysis, and internal investment approvals, through launch planning, hiring, system configuration, training, and go-live readiness. L&E does not stop at planning or approvals. We make decisions, drive execution on the ground, and build Amazon Japan’s operations as real, operating sites.
Spanning from First Mile to Last Mile, L&E plays a central role in driving Launch & Expansion across JP Ops.

L&E is currently composed of the following teams:
Core Planning and Execution (CPE)
CPE manages the Last Mile Core network composed of DS, XPT, and AMPL, covering new launches, closures, and network configuration changes.
The team leads end-to-end execution, including site selection, investment business case design, internal approvals, and start-up execution, while optimizing the network from a mid- to long-term perspective.
— A team that designs, implements, and optimizes the Last Mile Core network with a long-term view.
SSD Planning and Execution (SPE)
SPE owns SSD and AMZL+ projects from launch through closure. To support the growth of Same-Day Delivery, the team drives project execution that balances speed with repeatability and scalability.
— A team that rapidly scales the Same-Day Delivery network, a key growth area.
Retrofit, Expansion and Initiative (REI)
REI leads end-to-end execution for new and emerging initiatives, with a primary focus on Quick Commerce (QC). Working closely with global teams, REI scales these initiatives in Japan and establishes sustainable standards, including new programs such as Amazon Storage Unit (ASU).
— A team that turns concepts into viable, scalable businesses.
Launch Configuration and Verification (LCV)
LCV is responsible for system configuration and verification across all Last Mile node types. With a strong focus on “Right First Time,” the team supports reliable start-ups with a target of zero DPMO at launch.
— A team that ensures successful launches through robust system design and verification.
Project Management Office (PMO)
PMO operates horizontally across L&E, governing SOPs and playbooks, monitoring project progress, and managing PMIS to ensure execution discipline and visibility.
— A team that raises execution quality across L&E through standardization and continuous improvement.

Career Path
What makes L&E unique is that we do not simply sit between strategy and execution—we own both.
Few organizations within Amazon offer the opportunity to lead end-to-end, from upstream decisions such as network strategy and investment prioritization to on-the-ground execution and operational stabilization.
In L&E, you are not confined to a single site or function. You operate with a network-wide perspective across Japan Operations, constantly balancing local execution with system-level optimization.
This naturally builds the ability to think and decide not in silos, but in terms of overall impact.
With high ownership and accountability, L&E provides hands-on experience in driving complex, ambiguous projects to completion.
This experience accelerates growth not only as a project manager, but as a future leader who can shape and execute strategy.
For those who want to move beyond “delivering tasks” and instead define, decide, and build what comes next, L&E offers a uniquely dense and rewarding environment.

・Act as the Point of Contact (POC) for all launch activities from facility configuration preparation through Day 1 operational start for new QC sites
・Manage readiness status necessary for Day 1 success, including UTR/OTR fill rate monitoring, training compliance, and safety and compliance requirements
・Oversee on-site construction progress, handover from construction teams, and configuration testing to ensure all prerequisites for safe and efficient operational start are met
・Track readiness metrics, and ensure ramp-up plans are aligned with QC Planning and Operations

Launch Progress Management and Risk Response

Process Standardization and Improvement
・Drive standardization of launch processes with reproducibility and scalability for future expansion
・Establish best practices and achieve continuous improvement in a high-uncertainty environment within a new business domain

- Bachelor's degree

title: Controls Engineer, ADC
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptable power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph and satisfy other security related requirements.

Key job responsibilities
- Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.
- Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center.
- Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.
- Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
- Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
- Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.
- Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers.
- Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management.
- Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
- Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
- Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
- Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
- Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.
- Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation and/or under construction data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of industrial controls and automation experience
- 2+ years of general contractor and vendor management work (request for proposals, bidding, change orders, quality control, RFI/submittal tracking) associated with construction and project execution experience
- Experience with Industrial control systems, both hardware and software
- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or an equivalent engineering science plus 3+ years of relevant controls experience, OR 8+ years of relevant controls experience in lieu of a degree.
- Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret with SCI eligibility or above

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering or a related field
- Experience designing, configuring, programming, installing, troubleshooting or servicing HVAC Controls or Electrical SCADA systems application specific controllers, software and networks.
- Experiencing using common industrial communication protocols (MQTT, BACnet and/or MODBUS).
- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Ability to manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements, and navigate difficult situations.
- Experience designing data centers or critical MEP infrastructure
- Registered as a Professional Engineer (PE), or certified Project Management Professional (PMP).
- Prior AWS/Amazon experience
- 4+ Yr. Military Service
